ModMetaData.name: Beef Eaters Renew
ModMetaData.author: TheGoofyOne - 1.6 port: nelim
ModMetaData.description:
The Belgian blue cow and the pygmy beefalo, brought forward to RimWorld 1.6. One is all meat and no speed; the other is a muffalo that fits in a pen.
I am not the author of this mod. Both animals are TheGoofyOne's; all I did was the work needed to make them run on 1.6. Credit goes to them, mistakes in the update are mine. If they come back to it, or ask me to take this down, it comes down.
Original mod: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1988048034 - last supporting 1.4, last updated in March 2023. Abandoned, not withdrawn.
WHAT IT ADDS
Two livestock animals.
The Belgian blue cow is the double-muscled breed, and the stats say so: body size 6.0, the largest thing in most colonies, and a move speed of 0.8, slower than a walking colonist. Wildness 0.05, which is as close to born-tame as the game allows. Milkable.
The pygmy beefalo is a muffalo scaled down to body size 1.0 rather than 2.7: fifteen years, move speed 4.2, wildness 0.5, trainable to Advanced, milkable and shearable for muffalo wool. A pen animal rather than a caravan animal.
An Animal Gear patch ships with them, guarded so that it only applies when that mod is present.
WHAT CHANGED IN THE 1.6 UPDATE
Two lines, the same line twice. Wildness stopped being a field of RaceProperties in 1.6 and became a StatDef declared under statBases. The old form is not an error, it is simply never read, and the stat defaults to -1, outside the range the game uses - so the cow written to be nearly born-tame at 0.05 and the beefalo at 0.5 both behaved like anything else.
No balance value was changed.
Content mod: removing it mid-save will lose any Belgian blue cow or pygmy beefalo already in play.
Source, changelog and the full account of the port: https://github.com/vbardales/Rimworld-Beef-Eaters-Renew
The original states no licence anywhere - no file, nothing in its About, no repository, nothing on its Workshop page. This port therefore rests on the Workshop's own custom for abandoned mods: named credit to the author, and a takedown on request.
If I do not answer within a reasonable time after being contacted, anyone may freely update this or any other of my mods, including publishing a continuation of it. All credit must be preserved.
The update work was done with the help of an AI assistant (Claude, by Anthropic).
